name: The Sargasso Corridor
summary: Links the polar anchor and Bermuda. The MMS associates this corridor with the North Atlantic, the Sargasso Sea, and northern ice-and-mist traditions.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Hyperborean Corridor
summary: Links the polar anchor and Algerian node. The MMS reads northern European megalithic traditions, including Stonehenge and Orkney, through this corridor.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Shamanic Spine
summary: Links the polar anchor and Indus Valley. The MMS connects this corridor with Eurasian shamanic traditions, the Altai, drums, and world-tree cosmologies.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Dragon’s Spine
summary: Links the polar anchor and Devil’s Sea. The MMS associates this corridor with East Asian dragon traditions, geomancy, and sacred mountains.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Raven Road
summary: Links the polar anchor and Hawaii. The MMS reads Pacific Northwest Raven traditions, totem poles, and Hawaiian cultural practices through this corridor.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Antarctic Transmission
summary: Links the Antarctic anchor and South Atlantic node. The MMS associates this corridor with the Southern Ocean and southern polar mythology.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Bone Road
summary: Links the Antarctic anchor and Zimbabwe/Karoo. The MMS connects this corridor with the Karoo fossil record and Great Zimbabwe.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Southern Deep
summary: Links the Antarctic anchor and Wharton Basin. The MMS associates this corridor with the deep Southern and Indian Oceans.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Songline Root
summary: Links the Antarctic anchor and Loyalty Islands. The MMS interprets this corridor as a southern root of its Australian songline axis.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Navel Cord
summary: Links the Antarctic anchor and Easter Island. The MMS connects its interpretation with Rapa Nui’s Navel of the World name and the southern Pacific.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Atlantean Seam
summary: Links Bermuda and the Algerian node. The MMS associates this corridor with the Azores, Atlantic tectonic geography, and Atlantean narratives.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Cradle Road
summary: Links the Algerian node and Indus Valley. The MMS connects this corridor with Egypt, the Fertile Crescent, the Levant, and ancient civilizations.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Himalayan Bridge
summary: Links the Indus Valley and Devil’s Sea. The MMS associates this corridor with the Himalayas, Tibet, and contemplative mountain traditions.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Pacific River
summary: Links Devil’s Sea and Hawaii. The MMS connects this corridor with North Pacific circulation and the Kuroshio Current.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Turtle’s Back
summary: Links Hawaii and Bermuda. The MMS interprets North American Turtle Island narratives in relation to this connection.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Patagonian Gate
summary: Links the South Atlantic node and Easter Island. The MMS associates this corridor with Patagonia and the archaeological record of southern South America.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Polynesian Highway
summary: Links Easter Island and Loyalty Islands. The MMS connects this corridor with Polynesian wayfinding and Pacific settlement traditions.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Songline Spine
summary: Links Loyalty Islands and Wharton Basin. The MMS interprets this connection as the east–west axis of its Australian songline model.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Kerguelen Line
summary: Links Wharton Basin and Zimbabwe/Karoo. The MMS associates this corridor with the southern Indian Ocean and Kerguelen Plateau.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The South Atlantic Anomaly Line
summary: Links Zimbabwe/Karoo and the South Atlantic node. The MMS discusses the South Atlantic magnetic anomaly in relation to this corridor.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Middle Passage
summary: Links Bermuda and the South Atlantic node. The MMS connects this corridor with Caribbean and African diaspora traditions and the history of forced Atlantic crossings.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Drake Corridor
summary: Links Bermuda and Easter Island. The MMS associates this corridor with South American traditions, the Andes, and the Drake Passage.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Trade Wind Road
summary: Links the Algerian and South Atlantic nodes. The MMS connects this corridor with Atlantic trade winds, maritime routes, and African diaspora history.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Great Rift
summary: Links the Algerian node and Zimbabwe/Karoo. The MMS interprets the East African Rift and human origins in relation to this connection.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Dhow Road
summary: Links the Indus Valley and Zimbabwe/Karoo. The MMS associates this corridor with dhow routes, Indian Ocean exchange, and Swahili Coast cultures.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Monsoon Bridge
summary: Links the Indus Valley and Wharton Basin. The MMS connects this corridor with monsoon cycles and maritime exchange across the Indian Ocean.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Wallace Line
summary: Links Devil’s Sea and Wharton Basin. The MMS interprets Southeast Asian island geography and the Wallace biogeographic boundary in relation to this corridor.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Stick Chart Road
summary: Links Devil’s Sea and Loyalty Islands. The MMS associates this corridor with Micronesian wave piloting and Marshall Islands stick-chart navigation.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Polynesian Triangle’s Western Arm
summary: Links Hawaii and Loyalty Islands. The MMS interprets this connection as the western arm of its Polynesian navigation triangle.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas

name: The Long Voyage
summary: Links Hawaii and Easter Island. The MMS connects this corridor with long-distance Polynesian navigation across the central Pacific.
source: MMS v37 section 4.8; Myathe Magick Atlas
